# Statistical analysis report

*Generated by `write_report.py` on 2026-08-23. Every number below is computed at build time — none is typed by hand.*

> **This is a SIMULATED trial.** No participant, site, or investigator exists. The purpose is to verify that the methods recover a hazard ratio that was planted in the generator, not to report a finding about any therapy.

## 1. Analysis populations

```
Assessed for eligibility                     n = 1,251
  Excluded                                   n = 351
    did not meet inclusion criteria          n = 279
    declined to participate                  n = 72
Randomised                                   n = 900

  Treatment
    Allocated to intervention                n = 461
      Did not receive intervention           n = 10
      Discontinued: withdrew consent         n = 20
      Discontinued: lost to follow-up        n = 12
    Completed follow-up                      n = 419
    Analysed (ITT)                           n = 461
    Analysed (per protocol)                  n = 431

  Control
    Allocated to intervention                n = 439
      Did not receive intervention           n = 7
      Discontinued: withdrew consent         n = 14
      Discontinued: lost to follow-up        n = 8
    Completed follow-up                      n = 410
    Analysed (ITT)                           n = 439
    Analysed (per protocol)                  n = 418

```

The accounting closes: every randomised participant appears in exactly one terminal state, and each stage sums to the one above it. That invariant is the only part of this diagram that would still mean something on real data — **the attrition numbers here are chosen, not observed**, because a simulated trial has no screening log and no withdrawal process.

**Primary analysis is intention to treat.** Every randomised participant is analysed in the arm they were *assigned*, regardless of what they received. Per-protocol is reported as a sensitivity analysis only, and it is **the biased one**: adherence is a post-randomisation outcome, so conditioning on it reintroduces exactly the confounding randomisation was there to remove.

## 2. Primary endpoint: overall survival

| | Treatment | Control |
|---|---|---|
| n | 461 | 439 |
| events | 338 | 353 |
| median survival (months) | 13.8 (12.0–15.1) | 10.2 (8.9–11.8) |

Log-rank χ² = 11.29 on 1 df, p = 7.81e-04 (observed 338 vs expected 381.8 events in the treatment arm).

Intervals are **Brookmeyer–Crowley**, inverted from the Greenwood variance on the log(−log S) scale. A median is a quantile of a step function, so its sampling distribution is not symmetric and ±1.96 SE is the wrong *shape*, not merely imprecise — the confidence set is every time at which S(t)=0.5 would not be rejected. The log(−log) transform is not decoration: a plain-scale interval can extend past 0 or 1, and an interval containing “survival probability 1.04” tells the reader the method was wrong rather than the data. An upper bound reported as `None` means the confidence set is **open above**, which is the honest answer when the curve never falls far enough to reject S(t)=0.5 later; reporting the largest observed time instead would present a made-up number as an estimate.

## 3. Adjusted analysis: Cox proportional hazards

| covariate | HR | 95% CI | p |
|---|---|---|---|
| Treatment (vs control) | 0.743 | 0.640–0.863 | 1.02e-04 |
| Age (per decade) | 1.232 | 1.154–1.316 | 4.80e-10 |
| Stage (advanced) | 2.069 | 1.773–2.414 | 2.44e-20 |

Planted treatment HR: **0.7**. Estimated: **0.743** (0.640–0.863).

### Tie handling

Efron (default): HR 0.7430. Breslow: HR 0.7430. Events sharing a time: **0.0%**.

**The two agree to the digit here, and that is expected**: this generator produces continuous event times, so there are no ties and the two expressions are identical. Reporting the comparison on this data alone would show nothing. `run_ties.py` therefore rounds the same event times onto coarser grids — daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly — which is not an artificial manipulation: trial data arrives on a day grid and registry and claims data arrive on a month grid.

Both are approximations to the exact marginal likelihood over orderings within a tied event time. Breslow uses the full risk set for every death in a tied set, double-counting subjects who have already failed, which inflates the denominator and **biases coefficients toward the null**. `run_ties.py` measures this against the planted HR across event-time grids: at monthly rounding Breslow drifts +0.0059 toward the null and Efron +0.0001; at quarterly, +0.0179 against +0.0001. Attenuation understates a treatment benefit — conservative — and understates a **harm** signal by exactly as much, which is not.

## 4. Proportional hazards assumption

| covariate | ρ (Schoenfeld vs ranked time) | χ² | p |
|---|---|---|---|
| Treatment (vs control) | +0.001 | 0.00 | 0.985 |
| Age (per decade) | +0.046 | 1.43 | 0.231 |
| Stage (advanced) | -0.007 | 0.04 | 0.846 |

Treatment-covariate test: ρ = +0.001, p = 0.985 (n = 691 events).

Checked **before** the hazard ratio is interpreted, not after. A hazard ratio under non-proportional hazards is a weighted average of a changing effect, with weights determined by the censoring distribution — it is a number, but not the number anyone thinks they are reading. This is a simplified Grambsch–Therneau: correlation of unscaled Schoenfeld residuals with ranked time, not the scaled residuals with full variance–covariance treatment.

## 5. Restricted mean survival time

RMST difference at τ = 36 months: **+2.68 months** (+1.11, +4.22).

Reported alongside the hazard ratio because RMST requires no proportionality assumption and is interpretable without one: it is months of life gained over a stated horizon. τ must be pre-specified — choosing it after seeing the curves is a garden of forking paths, since every τ gives a different answer.

## 6. Limitations

- **Simulated data.** Exponential baseline hazard, no crossover, no missing covariates, no protocol deviations, no non-proportional baseline. The methods are verified against a planted truth; nothing here shows they survive real data.
- **The CONSORT attrition is chosen, not observed** — see §1.
- **Robust and clustered standard errors are available but not applied to the primary analysis**, because this trial has no site structure to cluster on — see src/inference.py, which measures that clustering only widens the interval when the covariate is CLUSTER-LEVEL.
- **No multiplicity handling**, no interim analysis, no alpha spending. The p-values are nominal.
- **Stratified Cox pools per-stratum estimates by inverse variance** rather than maximising a single stratified partial likelihood.
- **Fine–Gray uses a simplified IPCW scheme** — right-censoring-complete weights, no left truncation, no time-varying weights.
- **No bootstrap or robust standard errors, and no clustering.**
